newsitem.title: UK: Palm oil outlook weak, China business supports soft.
newsitem.headline: Palm oil outlook weak, China business supports soft.

text.p: Poor fundamentals and weak export demand are expected to weigh on palm oil prices during the coming weeks, while business to China is underpinning soft oils on the European vegetable oil market.
Traders said palm oil is coming into its peak production months but remains too expensive against other oils.
"It's a real surprise to everyone that palm oil has held up so well when it has not been competitive for some months, said one trader.
Traders said they expected a further downturn in palm oil prices unless buying from China, Pakistan and India emerges over the next couple of weeks.
Recent export figures released by Malaysian cargo surveyor Societe General de Surveillance (SGS) were queried by traders.
On Monday SGS put local export during the first 25 days of May at 547,382 tonnes against 549,976 during the same period in April.
However, traders in Europe and Asia said the figures were too high.
Soft oils remain steady with some tightness in supply being attributed to buying by China.
Figures released by the Chinese customs offices put imports of rape oil from the Netherlands at 14,220 tonnes during April.
"We don't know how much of the material was bought last year and has been held in store and how much is new business." said one trader.
"With China you don't find out what's going on until weeks after the event," the trader added.
Coconut oil prices look set to go lower after the recent concerns over shipment delays have been pushed into the background.
Traders said they felt that stories of tight supplies and shipment delays may have been over-played.
"I don't think things are as bad as some people would like us to think," said one.
Among industrial oils castor oil look's set to ease in the coming weeks with possible return of Brazil as an exporter to the market.
Traders estimate that Brazil could have around 10,000 to 15,000 tonnes of oil to export after being a net importer for the last three years.

Traders added that demand from China, another producer, appears to be drying up which would leave India, the world biggest producer, facing competition for the total world market of some 200,000 to 210,000 tonnes.
India is estimated to have around 200,000 to 210,000 tonnes of castor oil to export, which includes a carryover of 30,000 tonnes from last year.
"India had had a monopoly of the market for sometime so it good to see other countries coming in," said one trader.
